title: queue.item.v1: one queued message of a session
description: PUBLIC record. A message a user queued for a session. order is given when the item is made and never changes; items are delivered in that order. delivery 'next_turn' sends it as the next turn once the current one ends; 'steer' sends it into the turn in progress where the driver can take input mid-turn, and otherwise interrupts and then sends. The item can be edited (queue.update) or withdrawn (queue.cancel) ONLY while its state is 'queued'; each edit raises revision. 'delivering' means the daemon has COMMITTED its intent to deliver the item: the delivery_id is minted and stored and the item can no longer be edited or withdrawn. That commit comes BEFORE anything is written toward the engine, never after: a crash between the commit and the write leaves 'delivering', never 'queued', so a restart never sends anything a second time. While it is 'delivering' the daemon has not yet seen the engine take it. 'delivered' means an event from the engine named that delivery_id; turn_id is then the turn the item became. At a restart, an item still 'delivering' with no engine event naming its delivery_id becomes 'outcome_unknown': it is shown to the user and is never sent again by itself. One database commit cannot make delivery to an engine happen exactly once; this record says honestly which of the three it was. 'delivered', 'cancelled' and 'outcome_unknown' are final.

delivery_id.description: The id of the delivery attempt; null until delivery begins.

turn_id.description: The turn a delivered item became; null until then.
